headline: Nvidia-backed startup Upscale AI has launched Token Fabric, a network platform meant to link AI chips from competing makers.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a product launch with early-access timing and revenue hopes, not yet proven.
importance_line: It gives data-centre operators a way to avoid being locked into one vendor's chip links such as Nvidia's NVLink, though Token Fabric itself uses Nvidia's Spectrum-X switch chips on the scale-out side and the revenue figures are the CEO's expectation.
summary: Reuters reports, as relayed by The Next Web, that Upscale AI, a Santa Clara networking startup backed by Nvidia, launched Token Fabric on 8 Oct 2026, a platform built on open standards that connects AI chips from different suppliers within and across data-centre racks. The first part is due in the fourth quarter and general availability in early 2027, and chief executive Barun Kar expects Token Fabric revenue of tens of millions of dollars next year, possibly reaching the low hundreds of millions.
